newsitem.title: USA: FORECAST - Defense company profits seen slowing.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Defense company profits seen slowing.

text.p: The happy days of double- digit earnings per share growth for defense and aerospace companies may be coming to an end as profits margins appear to be dwindling from their recent highs.

"This is the first quarter in about three years that all the earnings estimates are less than double digits," said John Modzelewski, industry analyst at PaineWebber Inc. "Earnings per share gains seem to be slowing."
Earnings per share, year-over-year, have grown by about 10-12 percent annually in recent years.
Raytheon Co has pre-announced that it expects a 15 percent drop in operating earnings for the year.
"Raytheon may be a precursor to other disappointments in the next six to 12 months," Modzelewski said.
"A lot of other companies in the defense industry are going to show earnings disappointments, in time," he added.
Modzelewski predicts the industry will show earnings per share growth of about eight percent this quarter.
"The average defense company (profit margins) are at a historical high," he said. "You don't have any more room to expand margins...in fact they're going down."
Paul Nesbit of JSA Research agrees.
"Margin improvement rate is slowing a bit," he said. "Most of these companies...are reaching a point of fairly flat revenues."

Nesbit sees earnings per share growth flat for Litton Industries Inc, growing at about five percent for Hughes Electronics Corp and Lockheed Martin Corp, and at about seven percent for General Dynamics Corp and B.F. Goodrich Co.
Nesbit said that companies that merged in the past few years will see some consolidation savings for some time to come.
"We still have a lot more juice left in the industry from consolidations savings and associated margin improvements," said Jon Kutler of Quarterdeck Investment Partners.
"The trend is down, but I wouldn't be so quick to write off the sector."
Kutler said investors seeking value should look to professional services and information services companies.
Stock prices for these small companies, which provide a variety of outsourcing and software services to government agencies could see rapid growth, he said.
"You'll see a tremendous increase in their relative price-earnings ratios," he said.

Kutler said that companies providing the same services to the private sector trade at revenue multiples about four times higher than companies like Logicon Inc, Government Technology Services Inc and Tracor Inc. That discrepancy should correct over time, he said.

The past quarter has seen merger and acquisition activity continuing at a brisk pace. Rockwell International Corp sold its space and defense business to Boeing Co for $3.2 billion and Hughes signed a $3 billion pact to merge its satellite services with those of PanAmSat Corp, while numerous smaller deals have also been sealed.

That could continue this quarter with all eyes still on McDonnell Douglas Corp, which is yet to make a major acquisition. Names repeatedly metioned as potential targets are Hughes, Raytheon and Northrop Grumman Corp.
Nesbit said General Dynamics, Litton, Alliant Techsystems Inc, McDonnell Douglas and Raytheon could all be active buyers in the coming months.
Kutler sees the next wave of mergers coming in 1997 from divesting unwanted parts of companies that merged in the past two years and smaller cross-border U.S./European deals.
